newsitem.title: USA: Occidental says it has strengthened controls.
newsitem.headline: Occidental says it has strengthened controls.

text.p: Occidental Petroleum Corp, responding to a news article about its dealings with government agencies and businessmen in a number of countries, said early Monday that it has strengthened internal controls.

The company in its statement did not directly address the issues raised by the Wall Street Journal article in Monday's electronic edition. A company spokesman did not immediately return a telephone call seeking further comment.
However, George Nolley, the chairman of the Occidental board's audit committee, said in the statement that the issues raised by the Journal were reviewed in the past year.

"We believe that the process utilized to review such issues is proper and in the best interests of the company and its shareholders," Nolley said. "As part of its review, the audit committee recommended that additional policies and procedures be adopted in order to strengthen internal controls."
He said that those "enhanced controls" have been implemented by Occidental and its subsidiaries. The company did not disclose what kinds of controls were implemented.
The Journal said the lawyers have looked at records involving Occidental's dealings in Congo, Qatar, Bangladesh, Yemen, Malaysia and Russia, as well as other countries.
The Journal, citing unnamed sources it said were familiar with the matter, said the inquiry has found instances of questionable overseas transactions and lax financial procedures.

The Journal said the lawyers have concentrated on who authorized consulting payments and "finders fees" that some current and former company executives contend were not linked to identifiable services.

In addition, the lawyers have focused on some apparent discrepancies between the contract language signed by some middlemen and the work they performed for Occidental, the Journal quoted unnamed sources as saying.
